newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on late short-squeezing.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on late short-squeezing.

text.p: Key three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures surged late Wednesday as short-squeezing emerged from those who had sold in the recent fall.

Underlined sentiment had improved after the central bank refrained from its regular morning operation. The U.S. Federal Reserve's 0.25 point increase in interest rates might have dampened Euroyen futures if the Bank of Japan (BOJ) had not maintained its accommodative credit stance for a second day.

The key December contract's sudden rally in late afternoon was triggered by speculative buying, probably from foreigners, at around 99.04, traders said. It was a half-way recovery from December's recent fall from 99.24 to 98.81, traders said.
The December settled up 0.10 at 99.06 after rising to 99.08. Turnover was an active 115,587 contracts.
"Since the BOJ maintained its accommodative credit stance this morning (after a rise in U.S. interest rates), we all knew that Japan is Japan," a city bank dealer said.
"But breaking through a resistance point at around 99.04 resulted in a further rise due to short-squeezing," he added.
By not conducting an operation at 0020 GMT, the BOJ left the money market in surplus by an estimated 110 billion yen.
Another supportive factor was the easing of cash market interest rates as banks' demand for funds before the fiscal year-end subsided after peaking on Tuesday, traders said.
"Those who had sold the December to hedge in light of the recent rate rise in the interest rate swap (IRS) market started to buy back," said another city bank dealer.
Wednesday's fall in interest rates in the SWAP and cash Euroyen markets confirmed a view that banks' seasonal fund-raising demand had peaked, traders said.
In the open market, one-month certificates of deposit (CD), often a major instrument to raise funds covering the fiscal year-end, were issued for the first time since March 3.
"Both sides came closer today after demand for the fiscal year-end hit a peak on Tuesday," said another city bank dealer.
About 100 billion yen in CDs were issued at 0.61 percent, the highest rate since March 18, 1996. The key three-month CD rate fell to 0.59 percent from Tuesday's 0.60 percent.
The short-end benchmark overnight call rate fell to around 0.51 percent from Tuesday's weighed average of 0.53 percent. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3342-8570
